questions.question: What percentage of adults worldwide gamble at least once a year?
questions.answer: 60% - Around 60% of adults globally participate in some form of gambling annually, from lotteries to casinos.

questions.question: True or False: Online gambling is now larger than all physical casinos combined.
questions.answer: False - Online gambling is rapidly growing but still slightly smaller than the total physical casino market.

questions.question: Which country spends the most money per person on gambling?
questions.answer: Australia - Australians lose more per capita to gambling than any other nation, averaging over $1,000 per adult per year.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of gamblers develop a gambling problem?
questions.answer: 1-2% - Studies show about 1–2% of gamblers develop serious gambling addiction symptoms.

questions.question: True or False: Slot machines are designed to make players feel like they’re winning even when they’re losing.
questions.answer: True - Many slot machines use 'near-miss' effects and sounds to simulate frequent wins.

questions.question: How much money does the global gambling industry generate each year (as of 2024)?
questions.answer: $300 billion - The worldwide gambling market is estimated at roughly $300 billion annually.

questions.question: Which age group is statistically the most likely to gamble?
questions.answer: Young Adults (20–35) - Young adults are the most active gamblers, especially in online platforms and sports betting.

questions.question: True or False: Most gamblers win money over time if they play skill-based games like poker.
questions.answer: False - Even in skill-based games, the majority of players lose money over time due to the house edge and skill differences.

questions.question: What’s the most popular form of gambling worldwide?
questions.answer: Lotteries - Lotteries are the most common form of gambling, played by over 60% of adults in many countries.

questions.question: True or False: Problem gambling rates increase significantly when gambling is easily accessible online.
questions.answer: True - Studies show accessibility and constant availability increase problem gambling rates.

questions.question: What percentage of casino revenue typically comes from problem gamblers?
questions.answer: 25% - Roughly a quarter of casino revenue comes from people who gamble more than they can afford.

questions.question: Which gambling activity has the lowest odds of winning for players?
questions.answer: Lottery - The odds of winning major lottery jackpots can be as low as 1 in 300 million.

questions.question: True or False: The brain releases dopamine during both wins and near-misses.
questions.answer: True - Neuroscience shows that near-misses trigger the same dopamine response as actual wins, reinforcing play.

questions.question: In what year did online gambling first become available to the public?
questions.answer: 1994 - The first online casino was launched in 1994 after Antigua and Barbuda passed the Free Trade & Processing Act.

questions.question: True or False: More people gamble on their phones than on computers today.
questions.answer: True - Mobile gambling has overtaken desktop play due to convenience and app-based platforms.
